Parlange, Ph.D., P.Eng., President DATE: June 26, 2025 SUBJECT: Discussion Item: Update on the Comprehensive Campus Plan Purpose of Submittal: To update the Committee on the progress of the Comprehensive Campus Plan (CCP). Points to Consider: In June of 2024 the University, with Sasaki, kicked off the Comprehensive Campus Plan. • Phase 1 - Discovery and Analysis was completed in October 2024. • Phase 2 - Planning Scenarios were mostly completed in January 2025. • Phase 3 - Campus Plan Development January 2025 - June 2025. • Phase 4 - Final Documentation (July 2025-September 2025). This presentation will provide an overview of the draft final plan, which is in support of the University’s strategic plan. This overview will discuss a framework for the redevelopment of campus, future vision for Kingston campus neighborhoods, open space and landscape opportunities, mobility and circulation strategies , and sustainability initiatives. This overview will also provide a vision for the Narragansett Bay Campus, building on its existing master plan. Feedback from the Board will be incorporated by Sasaki and the URI Planning team as they finalize the plan over the summer. The plan will be brought to the Board for approval in September. Parlange, Ph.D., P.Eng., President DATE: September 11, 2024 SUBJECT: Action Item: FY2026 Total Budget Request Purpose of Submittal: This is a request for the University of Rhode Island Board of Trustees to approve the FY2026 Total Budget Request for submission to the State Office of Management and Budget. Recommendation: I recommend that the University of Rhode Island Board of Trustees approve the FY2026 Total Budget Request for submission to the State Office of Management and Budget. Points to Consider: The FY2026 total budget request for URI is $1.13B. Within this, the FY2026 State General Appropriations request is $146.2M and includes the following components: FY25 Enacted Operating Budget $110.8M Anticipated Operating Shortfall $5.7M Current Service Level $21.6M Strategic Initiatives $13.6M Total $151.7 Anticipated tuition & fee/misc revenue ($5.5M) Total FY26 Budget Request $146.2M The FY2026 General Appropriations includes a $13.6M request for Strategic Initiatives, which includes the following critical operating budget components, in alignment with the Focus URI Strategic Plan: SP1: Broaden Our Impact (Life Sciences Faculty and remaining land-grant state support) $5.3M SP2: Enhance Student Achievement (Academic Advisors) $2.0M SP3: Foster an Inclusive Culture (Support for TD Program, National Guard & Tribal scholarship support) $2.3M SP4: Power the University of the Future (IT Modernization) $4.0M Total $13.6M

As a reminder, last year the Board of Trustees shifted final approval of tuition and fees to the February meeting to make better informed decisions, therefore this budget request assumes a baseline tuition increase of 3.0% and fee increase of 0.7% which will be revisited in February. Finally, the FY2026 URI total budget request includes a significant increase in State RICAP support ($45.2M, 88% over FY2025), as reflected in the Capital Improvement Plan approved by the Board in June 2024. Supporting Information: Please refer to the attached presentation. A few highlights are outlined below. x The University’s financial position for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2024, shows an increase in net position of $45.56 million, compared to an increase of $40.25 million in fiscal year 2023. x When reviewing the University’s condensed statement of revenues, expenses, and changes in net position, it is important to note that nonoperating revenue plays an important role in supporting the operations of the university.
The primary component of nonoperating revenues is State appropriations. x In fiscal year 2024, total operating revenues rose by $18.01 million, representing a 3.57% increase, compared to a 3.96% increase of $19.23 million in fiscal year 2023. x Total operating expenses for the University increased by $27.76 million or 6.0% in fiscal year 2024, compared to a .65% increase of $3.99 million in fiscal year 2023. x The State’s unrestricted appropriation represents the largest component of the University’s nonoperating revenues.

The University of Rhode Island is the State’s flagship land and sea grant research institution, with a commitment to urban initiatives.
A student-centered research institution, URI actively partners with other organizations globally and locally to advance knowledge and to develop informed residents and leaders.

URI is committed to high-quality education, community engagement, and solving the world’s most important challenges.
Situated on the traditional land and territories of the Narragansett Nation and the Niantic People, URI strives to create a diverse and inclusive environment for researchers, teachers, learners, and community members.
URI’s Strategic Plan, Focus URI 2023-2033, lays out the strategic vision for the University for the next decade, outlining four strategic priorities and the actions the University will take to achieve them: Strategic Priority 1: Broaden the University’s impact through a reinvigorated commitment to its land and sea grant missions and the State of Rhode Island Strategic Priority 2: Enhance student achievement by cultivating an engaged and inclusive learning environment.
Strategic Priority 3: Foster an inclusive, people-centered culture.
Strategic Priority 4: Implement leading-edge administrative and financial systems and practices to power the University of the future.
The University’s main campus encompasses approximately 1,400 acres in Kingston, RI, 30 miles south of Providence in the northeastern metropolitan corridor between New York and Boston.

The 165-acre Narragansett Bay Campus (the “Bay Campus”), located six miles to the east overlooking the west passage of the Narragansett Bay, is home to the Graduate School of Oceanography and the Ocean Engineering Department of the College of Engineering.
In Providence, the University offers degree programs and conducts research and outreach programs in various locations.
In the western section of the State, 20 miles from Kingston, the 2,300 acres of woods, fields, streams and ponds on the W.
Alton Jones Campus are the site of research by various principal investigators.
The University offers degree programs through the doctoral level with a combined enrollment of 17,351.
First year applications for Fall 2023 and Fall 2024 were 25,391 and 26,983, respectively.
The University of Rhode Island is governed by a Board of Trustees consisting of 17 members appointed by the Governor with the advice and consent of the Rhode Island Senate.
